business.title: TyphoonSat: A high-resolution satellite imagery dataset for tropical cyclone detection in the Northwest Pacific (2015-2024)
business.description: Tropical cyclones (TCs) in the Northwest Pacific pose significant threats to coastal regions, yet the lack of a standardized object-detection dataset hinders fair algorithm evaluation. We present TyphoonSat, a high-resolution satellite imagery dataset for TC detection spanning 2015–2024. It comprises 5390 Himawari-8/9 infrared cloud images (1601 × 1201 pixels, 5 km resolution) covering 100°E–180°E and 0°–60°N, with 7895 bounding-box annotations in YOLO format, derived from best-track records from the China Meteorological Administration (CMABST). The dataset supports coarse (all intensities regarded as one category) and fine-grained (six intensity levels) detection tasks. Benchmarks using YOLOv8 variants demonstrate strong performance for coarse detection (mAP@50 up to 0.923, CSI up to 0.791) and highlight challenges in distinguishing weak-to-moderate intensities, while SuperTY detection excels (CSI up to 0.609). This dataset provides a unified benchmark for TC detection and fosters advances in deep-learning-based meteorological remote sensing.

science.title: Paired Fundus and Optical Coherence Tomography Dataset for Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration
science.description: Accurate classification of macular neovascularization (MNV) subtypes and reliable prediction of anti-VEGF treatment response are essential for individualized management of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), yet existing public AMD-related datasets lack multimodal imaging with fine-grained, longitudinal annotations to support these tasks. Here we present PCO-nAMD, a rigorously curated dataset of Paired color fundus photography (CFP) and optical coherence tomography (OCT) images designed to facilitate multimodal research on MNV subtype classification and treatment response prediction in nAMD. The dataset comprises two subsets: PCO-nAMD_MNV provides paired baseline CFP and OCT images from 327 patients with expert-adjudicated labels for four MNV subtypes (Type 1, Type 2, Type 3, and Mix), while PCO-nAMD_Response, a subset of 101 patients, further incorporates annotated pre-treatment image biomarkers alongside four-tier treatment response labels (good, partial, poor, and non-response). To characterize dataset difficulty and benchmark its utility, we conducted evaluation experiments showing that both tasks remain highly challenging for state-of-the-art multimodal large language models (MLLMs), and that incorporating curated biomarker annotations alongside imaging data consistently yields the best performance in treatment response prediction for GPT-5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro.

science.title: Phospholipid remodeling of the cardiomyocyte membrane affects cardiac function
science.description: Membrane phospholipid (PL) remodeling has been linked to various mammalian metabolic and oncogenic pathologies, but its role in the heart remains elusive. Here, we investigated the role of PL remodeling in cardiac function. Lysophospholipid acyltransferase 7 (LPLAT7)/lysophosphatidylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (LPGAT1) remodels phosphatidylcholine (PC) and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), two major cardiac membrane PL species. Public functional genomics data revealed downregulation of LPLAT7/LPGAT1 gene expression in failing human hearts and murine cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocyte-specific Lplat7/Lpgat1-deficient male mice exhibited selective remodeling of cardiac PC and PE composition, including diminished stearic acid- and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)-enriched species. LPLAT7/LPGAT1 suppression induced myocardial contractile dysfunction associated with cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA) activation and abnormal calcium handling, partially rescued by pharmacological PKA inhibition. Conversely, Lplat7/Lpgat1 overexpression partially improved pressure overload-induced cardiac dysfunction with selective restoration of PC(40:6), a major stearic acid/DHA-enriched PC species. These findings highlight the contributory role of LPLAT7/LPGAT1-dependent membrane PL remodeling in cardiac function and heart failure. Cardiomyocyte LPLAT7/LPGAT1 regulates membrane phospholipid composition and cardiac function. Its loss reduces stearic acid- and DHA-enriched phosphatidylcholine and causes PKA activation, abnormal calcium handling, and contractile dysfunction, whereas overexpression partially improves pressure overload-induced dysfunction

science.title: Red-sensitive pigments in mantis shrimp eyes act as reversible light switches
science.description: With about 30 visual pigments, compared to just three in humans, mantis shrimp possess a visual system that remains a mystery. Researchers from ULiège and Humboldt University in Berlin have, for the first time, analyzed these pigments one by one and discovered that some detect red light that very few animals can perceive. This finding, published in Science Advances, has potential applications in optogenetics.
